To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the combination of a cinchonium-based catalyst and a phenolic acid as an auxiliary reagent allows for the development of a catalyst platform for the direct construction of chiral nonadjacent stereogenic centers in a single step.

a catalyst system based on the synergistic cooperation of cinchonium salts and phenolic proton donors enables the direct generation of complex chiral ams bearing two nonadjacently positioned stereocenters through asymmetric tandem reactions.

a synergistic catalyst system based on a cinchonium catalyst and a phenolic catalyst enables the direct asymmetric synthesis of chiral nonadjacent stereogenic amines by controlling the chemoselective reactivity of two distinct reaction intermediated in a tandem reaction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of catalysts to control the selectivity of multiple reaction intermediates in tandem reactions, thereby enabling the direct synthesis of complex chiral amina

the development of small molecule catalyst systems that can achieve precise control over the reaction mode for each reaction intermediate, thereby enabling asymmetric tandem reactions to be directly applied to the synthesis of complex chiral molecules.
the design of a catalyst system to control chemoselectivity, which enabled a direct asymmetric synthesis of chiral nonadjacent stereogenic centers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this paper describes the mechanistically guided design of a catalyst system to enable an efficient asymmetric tandem conjugate–addition protonation reaction cascade to directly transform simple achiral precursors to complex chiral amins bearing two nonadjacents stereocenters.

this work demonstrates the development of a catalyst that enables the asymmetric tandem reaction of two reaction intermediates to provide optically active nonadjacent stereogenic centers, which are present in many natural products and pharmaceuticals.

this paper describes the mechanistically-guided development of an asymmetric tandem reaction, employing a cinchonium phase-transfer catalyst in combination with a phenolic proton-donor catalyst, which enables the desired asymmetric conjugate addition/protonation pathway to occur in preference over numerous side reactions to provide a direct synthetic approach for the generation of optically-active amines bearing multiple stereocenters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we developed a small molecule catalyst inspired by biocatalysts to control the chemoreactivity of reaction intermediates in tandem reactions, which enabled the direct synthesis of chiral compounds with multiple nonadjacent stereogenic centers.
we have developed a small molecule catalyst that can mimic a number of traits of biocatslsts.
we developed a catalyst system to control how two distinct intermediates react in a tandem reaction to establish a new asymmetric conjugate addition-protonation reaction cascade.
The main takeaway from our work is that

by controlling chemoselectivity, a single catalyst system can achieve multiple reaction modes for two different reaction intermediates to enable the direct synthesis of complex chiral compounds from achiral precursors.

the synergistic cooperation between the proton donor catalyst and the phase-transfer catalyst is crucial for the control of the chemoselective pathway in asymmetric tandem reactions to generate chiral nonadjacent stereogenic centers.

by controlling the chemoselectivities of the two reaction intermediates in a tandem fashion, we could achieve a highly selective and efficient synthesis of chiral nonracemic amines bearing multiple stereocenters.
